messages:
nata: noticed a bundle size spike + runtime failure when deploying the pages-edge sample. runtime error in production: "TypeError: createClient is not a function" only after minified prod build. dev build fine.

ryan: can you paste the SDK package.json inside node_modules? ESM/CJS entries and sideEffects matter.

nata: sure, pasted from node_modules/redwood-sdk/package.json: 
"main": "dist/index.cjs.js", "module": "dist/index.esm.mjs", "sideEffects": false, "exports": {"import": "./dist/index.esm.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"}

lee: edge bundlers (esbuild/wrappers for pages) aggressively tree-shake when sideEffects=false. our runtime init file registers some global shims and does dynamic property injection — that looks like the victim.

anya: also seeing a mismatch in types: dist/index.d.ts declares `export default function createClient(...)` but runtime is `export function createClient(...)` (named). Consumers using `import createClient from 'redwood-sdk'` through TS config get incorrect emitted code for ESM.

ci-bot: CI note: recent canary build for sample-pages-edge shows +120KB gzipped delta after sdk@1.4.8 landed.

nata: quick workaround for customers deploying to edge: import the init module directly before named imports: 
```js
import 'redwood-sdk/dist/runtime/init.mjs';
import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk';
```
This forces bundlers to preserve the runtime file. ugly but small stopgap.

ryan: long term fixes we discussed: (a) keep `sideEffects: false` but whitelist runtime files: "sideEffects": ["./dist/runtime/init.mjs"] (b) add explicit re-export in esm entry: `export { createClient } from './runtime/createClient.mjs'` so static analysis sees it (c) fix .d.ts to use named export signature and add a test that builds the edge sample in production mode.

lee: alternative is to provide a tiny top-level shim file `dist/edge-compat.mjs` that imports and re-exports runtime helpers, and list that file in exports: {"import": "./dist/index.esm.mjs", "edge": "./dist/edge-compat.mjs"} — but that complicates the export map.

anya: agreed on types fix. i'll open a types-only PR to change `export default` -> `export declare function createClient(...)` and add a rollup of types test in our TypeScript CI job.

doc-writer: i'll add a short DevEx note for the migration guide explaining the temporary `import '.../init.mjs'` pattern and the upcoming patch. include example and reasons (tree-shaking).

nata: will open a patch PR that: updates package.json sideEffects to include runtime, adds explicit ESM re-export, updates d.ts, and adds a CI smoke build for pages/edge. will link PR here once open.

ci-bot: job started: sample-pages-edge-prod-smoke. will report back.

ryan: reminder: do NOT flip `sideEffects: true` for whole package — that'll prevent tree-shaking for consumers. only whitelist the exact files that are initialization-only.

nata: PR opened: #4387 (changes listed). running canary now.

ci-bot: canary result: PROD edge build green, runtime check `typeof createClient === 'function'` passed. size regression reverted.

anya: thanks all. follow-up work: add test coverage for both rollup and esbuild bundling modes, and add a short entry in SDK release notes explaining the change and why we whitelisted runtime files.
